headline: Nvidia jumps 31.5% as Jensen Huang returns as CEO, lifting the Nasdaq 6.5% in its best day since April 2025
subhead: The S&P 500 rose 4.7% to 7,237.2, ending a seven-session slide, gold gained 3.7% and WTI fell 4.2%; India, Hong Kong, Taiwan and European prices on this page are still from 20 Nov because the price feed had no 23 Nov data.

us.text: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO 11 days after he stepped down; the stock rose 31.5% to 165.05, its best day since 2003.
The S&P 500 rose 4.7% to 7,237.2 and the Nasdaq 6.5% to 24,089.6, ending a seven-session S&P losing streak.
New York Fed's Williams called inflation too high and left more hikes open; futures price about 98% odds of a December hike.

india.text: On 23 Nov the Sensex fell 1,483.7 points to 82,436.0 and Nifty ended at 25,349.7 as metals and PSU banks led losses.
FIIs net bought 5,673 crore rupees in cash on 23 Nov while DIIs net sold 2,760 crore, per provisional data.
The rupee traded near 92.92 per dollar on 23 Nov, easing slightly from a seven-month high as equities fell.

global.text: With Tokyo shut for a holiday on 23 Nov, the Kospi fell to a ten-month low while Taiwan's Taiex rebounded.
European stocks closed up nearly 2% on 23 Nov as chipmakers led a rebound from the AI rout.
WTI fell 4.2% to 80.48 dollars and Brent 6.1% to 86.95 as recovering Middle East supply fed surplus fears.

weekly.narrative: An AI unwind dominated the week: Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut failed to steady sentiment, Nvidia fell 22.9 percent and the Nasdaq 10.0 percent, its worst week since March 2020, while the S&P 500 lost 8.6 percent and closed in correction. Near-certain bets on a December Fed hike pushed gold down 8.1 percent and silver 14.4 percent to near 52-week lows, and bitcoin fell 5.8 percent toward its 2026 low. India stood apart as heavy foreign buying lifted the Nifty to a nine-month high of 25,800.6 and Bank Nifty to records, while Tokyo, Seoul and Frankfurt followed Wall Street lower. Next week is shortened by Thanksgiving and turns on US PCE inflation and GDP on 25 November, ahead of the Fed decision on 9 December.
